name: Bahrain (Behrain)
summary: Riverside town at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers, with handicraft markets and the trailhead for Daral and Saidgai lakes.

facts.text: The name means 'two rivers' for the Daral/Swat confluence.
facts.quote: due to its location at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers

facts.text: It is a base camp for the Daral and Saidgai lakes trail.
facts.quote: It also serves as a base camp for the trail that leads to the Daral and Saidgai lakes.

facts.text: It lies 60 km north of Mingora at 4,700 ft on the right bank of the Swat River.
facts.quote: 60 km north of Mingora at an elevation of 4,700 ft on the right bank of the Swat River

facts.text: It is known for riverside tourist resorts and local handicrafts.
facts.quote: It is known for its riverside tourist resorts, local handicrafts, and its view of the merging of the Daral and Swat rivers.

facts.text: Some houses have carved wooden doors, pillars and balconies.
facts.quote: Some of the houses have carved wooden doors, pillars and balconies.

access: N-95, 60 km north of Mingora; year-round road.

name: Barikot
summary: Gateway town to central Swat and base for the Bazira, Gumbat, Shingardar and Amluk-Dara sites.

timeline.event: Early-historic town founded
timeline.quote: Barikot is the location of an ancient citadel captured by Alexander the Great, with chalcolithic remains dating back to c. 1700 BC, and an early-historic period town dating back to c. 600 BC.

facts.text: Barikot lies on the middle course of the Swat River, about 20 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is located about 20 km (12 mi) away from Mingora and the Butkara Stupa.

facts.text: The entrance town to central Swat, with about 115,045 people.
facts.quote: It is the entrance town to the central Swat valley with a population of approximately 115,045 people.

facts.text: Site of an ancient citadel taken by Alexander; remains go back to c. 1700 BC.
facts.quote: Barikot is the location of an ancient citadel captured by Alexander the Great, with chalcolithic remains dating back to c. 1700 BC, and an early-historic period town dating back to c. 600 BC.

facts.text: Italian excavations found an Indo-Greek town from the time of King Menander I, 2nd century BC.
facts.quote: The Italian expeditions in the 1980s and 90s discovered an Indo-Greek town from around the time of King Menander I in the 2nd century BC.

access: N-95 from Chakdara/Mingora.

name: Daral Lake
summary: Amoeba-shaped glacial lake above Bahrain with a shepherds' mosque near its shore.

facts.text: It is accessible only during the summer.
facts.quote: Daral Lake is accessible only during the summer

facts.text: A shepherds' mosque stands near the lake.
facts.quote: Near the lake, there is an ancient mosque where shepherds and visitors offer their prayers

facts.text: The lake lies at 3,505.2 m (11,500 ft).
facts.quote: at an elevation of 3,505.2 m (11,500 ft)

facts.text: From Bahrain the trek takes three to four hours.
facts.quote: it can be accessed from Bahrain in three to four hours of trekking on bare mountains

facts.text: The lake looks like a giant amoeba.
facts.quote: The lake appears as a giant amoeba in shape.

access: Trek 4-5 h from Gabin Jabba or 3-4 h from Bahrain; June-Sept.

name: Dir (Dir Khas)
summary: Former capital of Dir state and Upper Dir seat, at the foot of Lowari Pass on the road to Chitral; the road to Kumrat leaves the main road here.

timeline.event: Dir state was fully incorporated into Pakistan.
timeline.quote: It was the capital of the former princely state of Dir, until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.

facts.text: At the base of Lowarai Pass on the road to Chitral.
facts.quote: It is at the base of the Lowarai Pass, the main road to Chitral.

facts.text: Founded in the 17th century.
facts.quote: Dir was founded in the 17th century.

facts.text: Dir was the capital of the princely state of Dir until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.
facts.quote: It was the capital of the former princely state of Dir, until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.

facts.text: The former royal palace stands on a hill above the city.
facts.quote: The former royal palace is on a hill above the city.

facts.text: The town lies along the Dir River, a tributary of the Panjkora.
facts.quote: It lies along the Dir River, a tributary of the Panjkora River.

access: N-45 from Chakdara/Timergara.

name: Fatehpur (Swat)
summary: Union council and small town on the Swat valley road between Madyan and Khwazakhela.

facts.text: Fatehpur is a union council of Upper Swat.
facts.quote: Fatehpur is an administrative unit, known as Union council, of Upper Swat District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.

access: On the main Swat valley road (N-95) north of Mingora.

name: Kanju
summary: Village on the Swat River just north of Mingora, known for peaches and for the Ayub Bridge river views; Saidu Sharif airport sits beside it.

facts.text: Kanju lies 3 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is 3 kilometres away from Mingora, the main city of Swat District, and about 5 kilometres from Saidu Sharif, the district's capital.

facts.text: Kanju peaches are widely known.
facts.quote: The peaches of Kanju and overall Swat are known all over Pakistan.

facts.text: Views of the Swat River from Ayub Bridge.
facts.quote: There are views of the river Swat from Ayub Bridge in Kanju.

facts.text: Saidu Sharif airport lies between Kanju and Dherai.
facts.quote: Saidu Sharif airport is situated between Kanju and Dherai.

access: On the Mingora-Kalam road.

name: Khwazakhela
summary: Second-largest commercial centre of Swat after Mingora, where shoppers from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla come to trade; junction town for the Shangla road.

timeline.event: The Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque was built near Khwazakhela by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.
timeline.quote: One important historical site in the area is the Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque, which was built in the 12th century by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.

facts.text: Second-largest commercial centre in Swat.
facts.quote: Khwazakhela is the second-largest commercial center in Swat after Mingora.

facts.text: Draws people from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla.
facts.quote: Many people from Kalam, Kohistan, and Shangla come here for shopping and business.

facts.text: The Lwar-e-Jamat mosque in the area dates to the 12th century.
facts.quote: One important historical site in the area is the Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque, which was built in the 12th century by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.

facts.text: It is well known for the graves of religious saints.
facts.quote: Khwazakhela is well known for the graves of religious saints (Awliya).

facts.text: It had a population of 57,113 in the 2023 census.
facts.quote: As of the 2023 census, Khwazakhela had a population of 57,113.

access: On the N-95 between Mingora and Madyan; all-year road.

name: Madyan
summary: Bustling Torwali-majority riverside town where the Chail and Swat valleys join; a dining and shopping stop and base for the Bahrain-Kalam road.

facts.text: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.
facts.quote: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.

facts.text: The Chail and Swat valleys join at Madyan.
facts.quote: The two valleys join at Madyan, 8 km below Bahrain.

facts.text: It stands at 1,321 m and has many hotels in all price ranges and some good tourist shopping.
facts.quote: at 1,321 m (4,335 feet) above sea level, but it is a larger town and has many hotels in all price ranges and some good tourist shopping.

facts.text: Shawls, embroidery, tribal jewellery, carved wood and coins are sold along the main street.
facts.quote: Antique and modern shawls, traditional embroidery, tribal jewellery, carved wood and antique or reproduced coins are sold along the main street.

facts.text: The central mosque has carved wooden pillars with elegant scroll capitals.
facts.quote: The central mosque at Madyan has carved wooden pillars with elegant scroll capitals

access: N-95 about 55 km from Mingora.

name: Manglawar (Manglor)
summary: Town at the mouth of the Malam Jabba road, earlier a capital of the Swat state, with Buddhist reliefs and a stupa in its side valleys.

facts.text: Manglawar is a former capital of the Kingdom of Swat.
facts.quote: of Swat District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan and former capital of Kingdom of Swat.

facts.text: Average altitude is 987 m.
facts.quote: with an average altitude of 987 meters (3,238.19 feet).

facts.text: The valley lies about 9 km north-east of Mingora.
facts.quote: Manglawar (or Manglor) valley in Pakistan is situated about 9 km to north east of Mingora

facts.text: Sultan Pakhal Swati founded the Kingdom of Swat with Manglawar as its capital.
facts.quote: Sultan Pakhal Swati founded Kingdom of Swat with capital as Manglawar.

facts.text: Has the second biggest rock-carved Buddha after Bamiyan, at Jahanabad.
facts.quote: it is having the second biggest rock carved Buddha statue (formally called as Budh Ghat) at Jahan Abad (Janabad) in Central Asia after Buddha of Bamiyan.

access: 12 km from Saidu Sharif; junction for Malam Jabba and Jahanabad.

name: Miandam
summary: Forested hill-station valley west of the Swat River at the foot of the Hindu Kush, with a WWF medicinal-plant project.

facts.text: It is about 55 km from Mingora.
facts.quote: It is located at a distance of 55 km away from Mingora the capital of Swat Valley

facts.text: A WWF project promotes sustainable harvesting of medicinal plants.
facts.quote: the town is the site of a World Wide Fund for Nature project promoting sustainable harvesting of medicinal plants

facts.text: It is a small summer resort 10 km up a steep side valley, an hour's drive from Saidu Sharif.
facts.quote: Miandam is a small summer resort 10 km (6 mi) up a steep side valley and 56 km (35 mi) from Saidu Sharif, making it an hour's drive.

facts.text: Miandam is a good place for walkers, with paths following the stream.
facts.quote: Miandam is a good place for walkers. Paths follow the stream

facts.text: Graveyards hold carved wooden grave posts with floral designs.
facts.quote: In the graveyards are carved wooden grave posts with floral designs

access: Paved road from Madyan/Mingora side; spring-autumn, snow in winter.

name: Mingora
summary: The largest city of Swat, beside Saidu Sharif, the district capital, on the Swat River. It is the base for the Butkara and Saidu Sharif Buddhist sites and the gateway for trips up-valley to Fizagat, Malam Jabba, Madyan and Kalam.

timeline.event: 475 Indo-Aryan graves excavated at Loe Banr, Butkara II and Matalai
timeline.quote: At Loe Banr, Butkara II and Matalai, Italian archaeologists unearthed 475 Indo-Aryan graves dated between 1520 and 170 BC and two horse skeletons.

timeline.event: Chinese monk Faxian reports a large Buddhist monastery at Mingora
timeline.quote: In Mingora, the 4th century Chinese Buddhist monk Faxian claimed to have seen the largest Buddhist monastery

timeline.event: Hindu Shahi rule ends with the rise of Mahmud Ghaznavi
timeline.quote: Hindu Shahi rule came to an end with the rise of the Muslim empire of Mahmud Ghaznavi in the 11th century.

timeline.event: Taliban take Mingora during the insurgency
timeline.quote: In 2007 during the rise of the Taliban insurgency, Mingora was invaded by the Taliban

facts.text: Mingora is the largest city of Malakand Division.
facts.quote: Mingora is the largest city and the epicenter of social, cultural, and economic activities in Malakand Division

facts.text: Third largest city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the Swat River.
facts.quote: Located on the Swat River, it is the third largest city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the 26th largest in Pakistan.

facts.text: The Butkara Stupa near Mingora is ringed by more than 200 votive stupas.
facts.quote: Excavations at the Butkara Stupa near Mingora revealed a large and imposing central stupa surrounded by more than 200 votive stupas

facts.text: Italian archaeologists found 475 Indo-Aryan graves here, dated 1520-170 BC.
facts.quote: At Loe Banr, Butkara II and Matalai, Italian archaeologists unearthed 475 Indo-Aryan graves dated between 1520 and 170 BC and two horse skeletons.

facts.text: A Gandhara grave culture site at Aligrama, near Saidu Sharif airport, dates to 1000 BC.
facts.quote: on the opposite side of the river Swat at Aligrama, near the Saidu Sharif airport, a site of Gandhara grave culture was discovered by the Italian archaeologists and dated to 1000 BC.

access: Main road hub; Swat Expressway/N-95 from Chakdara (about 40 km).

name: Saidu Sharif
summary: Former capital quarter of the princely state of Swat, adjoining Mingora; named after the Akhund of Swat (Saidu Baba). The state-era royal buildings, Jahanzeb College and the Swat Museum cluster here.

timeline.event: Settlement renamed Saidu Sharif (earlier Baligram) after Saidu Baba

facts.text: The older name was Baligram.
facts.quote: The older name of Saidu Sharif was Baligram.

facts.text: It is named for Saidu Baba.
facts.quote: It was named after Saidu Baba, a prominent leader of the former state of Swat.

facts.text: Capital of Swat District.
facts.quote: is the capital of the Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

facts.text: Hub of official buildings: Swat Museum, Saidu Baba's mausoleum, the Wali's palace and Butkara stupa remains.
facts.quote: Saidu Sharif is the hub of several official buildings, and archaeological sites such as the Swat Museum, the mausoleum of Saidu Baba, royal residential palace of the former Wali-e-Swat, and the archaeological remains of the Butkara Buddhist stupa.

facts.text: Jahanzeb College, the district's largest, was built in 1952.
facts.quote: the largest college in the district is P.G Jahanzeb College which was built in 1952.

access: Contiguous with Mingora.

name: Timergara
summary: Lower Dir district headquarters on the Panjkora, a transit town on the Chakdara-Dir road (N-45).

timeline.event: Indo-Aryan graves of this period excavated at Timergara
timeline.quote: The town is the site of excavated graves of Indo-Aryans, dating from 1500 to 600 BC.

facts.text: Lies at 823 m on the east bank of the Panjkora.
facts.quote: Timergara city is located on the east bank of the Panjkora River. It lies at an altitude of 823 metres (2,700 ft).

facts.text: District headquarters of Lower Dir.
facts.quote: is a city and the district headquarters of the Lower Dir district

facts.text: Excavated Indo-Aryan graves here date from 1500 to 600 BC.
facts.quote: The town is the site of excavated graves of Indo-Aryans, dating from 1500 to 600 BC.

facts.text: The excavated site of Balambat lies across the Panjkora.
facts.quote: On the west side of the Panjkora River is the excavated site of Balambat.

facts.text: Balambat finds include houses from 500 BC and fire altars.
facts.quote: Discoveries included houses dating from 500 BC and fire altars

access: N-45, between Chakdara and Dir.

name: Udegram (Odigram, ancient Ora)
summary: Village on the Swat River NW of Mingora on the site identified with Ora of Alexander's campaign, later a Hindu Shahi capital; hosts the Raja Gira castle and Ghaznavid mosque.

timeline.event: Alexander storms Odigram (Ora)
Hindu Shahi dynasty has its capital at Udigram

facts.text: Odigram is the site of the Ghaznavid-era mosque.
facts.quote: Odigram is the site of the Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque, one of the oldest in Pakistan.

facts.text: Hindu Shahis made their capital at Udigram.
facts.quote: who made their capital at Udigram in lower Swat

facts.text: Graves here and at Gogdara show two Gandhara grave culture phases, 1400-1100 and 1000-800 BCE.
facts.quote: New research, based on 34 excavated graves in Udegram, and in the nearby site of Gogdara, has uncovered two Gandhara grave culture burial phases, the first between 1400 and 1100 BCE, and the second from 1000 to 800 BCE

facts.text: Its Ghaznavid mosque dates to 1048-49 CE.
facts.quote: The Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque was built in the former Hindu Shahi capital of Odigram shortly after their defeat, and dates to 1048-49 CE.

access: 8 km NW of Mingora by road.

photos.attribution: Photo: Muhammad Zahir, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
photos.caption: The excavated Mahmud Ghaznavi mosque at Udegram

name: Amluk-Dara Stupa
summary: A large dome-shaped Buddhist stupa south of the Swat River, among the best-preserved in the valley, with a squarish plinth under a hemispherical dome visible for miles.

timeline.event: Stupa built
Discovered by Aurel Stein
Studied by Domenico Faccenna

facts.text: It was found by Aurel Stein in 1926.
facts.quote: The stupa was first discovered by a Hungarian-British archaeologist Sir Aurel Stein in 1926.

facts.text: The dome is 21 m across and 7 m tall.
facts.quote: a hemispherical dome measuring 7 meter in height and 21 meters in diameter

facts.text: It is unprotected and damaged by treasure hunters.
facts.quote: it is unprotected and is being damaged by treasure seekers.

facts.text: Described as the best example of a stupa in Swat.
facts.quote: Though it is the best example of a stupa in Swat, it is unprotected and is being damaged by treasure seekers.

facts.text: The base is a square plinth about 4 m thick.
facts.quote: The foundation of the stupa is a square plinth about 4 meters thick.

access: South side of the river near Barikot/Shamozai; road then short walk.

name: Bazira (Barikot Ghundai)
summary: The excavated ancient city at Barikot hill, identified with the Bazira stormed by Alexander in 327 BCE. Italian excavations since 1984 show occupation from the Bronze Age, a fortified city from the mid-first millennium BCE, an Indo-Greek wall and later Kushan and Buddhist phases.

timeline.event: First traces of human presence (pit remains)
Early-historic fortified town
Alexander the Great takes Bazira (identification with Barikot)
Italian Archaeological Mission (ISMEO) excavations

facts.text: The Italian mission has excavated Bazira since 1984.
facts.quote: has been excavating ruins of the ancient town of Bazira under Barikot since 1984.

facts.text: Greek accounts of Alexander's 327 BCE attack are identified with Odigram (Ora) and Barikot (Bazira).
facts.quote: In 327 BCE, Alexander the Great fought his way to Odigram and Barikot and stormed their battlements; in Greek accounts, these towns are identified as Ora and Bazira, respectively.

facts.text: The fortified urban settlement dates to about the mid-first millennium BCE.
facts.quote: the fortified urban settlement in Barikot (lower area and acropolis) was established around mid-first millennium BC.

facts.text: The earliest Buddhist apsidal temple was found here, in ancient Bazira.
facts.quote: announced the discovery of the earliest Buddhist apsidal temple in Barikot (the ancient Bazira)

access: Barikot, about 20 km SW of Mingora on the main road; hill site reachable on foot from the road.

name: Butkara I Stupa
summary: The largest excavated Buddhist stupa of the Swat plain, on the eastern edge of Mingora near Saidu Sharif. A core stupa of the Mauryan/early Indo-Greek period was encased five times by later enlargements and ringed by hundreds of votive stupas. Italian excavations from 1956 recovered much of the Gandharan sculpture now in the Swat Museum.

timeline.event: Original stupa built; later enlarged five times by encasing the earlier structure
Italian Archaeological Mission led by Domenico Faccenna excavates the stupa

facts.text: The stupa was probably built in the 2nd century BCE, with a possible Ashokan origin.
facts.quote: It may have been built by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, but it is generally dated slightly later to the 2nd century BCE.

facts.text: It was enlarged five times, each time by building over the previous structure.
facts.quote: The stupa was enlarged on five occasions during the following centuries

facts.text: Excavation by an Italian mission began in 1956.
facts.quote: led by archaeologist Domenico Faccenna from 1956

facts.text: The oldest core layer contained a coin of Chandragupta Maurya, supporting an early date.
facts.quote: The oldest core strata (GSt 1) revealed a coin of Chandragupta Maurya

facts.text: An Indo-Corinthian capital of a Buddhist devotee is dated to before 20 BCE.
facts.quote: An Indo-Corinthian capital representing a Buddhist devotee within foliage has been found which had a reliquary and a coin of Azes II buried at its base, securely dating the sculpture to earlier than 20 BCE.

access: Within Mingora/Saidu Sharif, about 1 km east of the Swat Museum; reachable by road year-round (flat, no hike).

summary: A smaller Buddhist stupa area with votive stupas, excavated in the same Italian programme as Butkara I and located about 1 km south-east of it, on the Mingora outskirts.

name: Chakdara Fort
summary: British-built hill fort commanding the Swat River crossing at the south entrance to Swat, on the site of an older Mughal fort and famed for its defence in 1897.

timeline.event: Mughals build a fort at Chakdara
British occupy and build the present fort
Besieged during the Siege of Malakand

facts.text: The Mughals built a fort in 1586; the British built the present one in 1896.
facts.quote: The Mughals built a fort here in 1586, occupied in 1895 by the British, who built the present fort in 1896

facts.text: It was besieged in 1897.
facts.quote: The Battle of Chakdara was a battle and siege of a British military fort by rebel Pashtun tribesmen during the Siege of Malakand in colonial British India's North West Frontier Province in 1897

facts.text: About 240 mostly Indian soldiers held the fort and signal tower.
facts.quote: A total of around 240 mostly Indian soldiers were stationed in the fortress and nearby signal tower.

name: Elum Ghar (Mount Ilam)

facts.text: It is the highest peak in the region, 2,800 m.
facts.quote: Elum Ghar, also known as Mount Elum, is a 2,800 metres (9,200 ft) high mountain located in the Swat and Buner districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Elum Ghar is the highest peak in the region, and is snow-covered most of the year.

facts.text: It was a significant Hindu pilgrimage site until 1947.
facts.quote: The mountain was a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus until 1947

access: Hike from Marghazar/Pir Baba side; 1-day trek, local guide advised.

facts.text: A Buddha is carved in rock beside the road to Mingora.
facts.quote: On the way to Mingora there is a statue of Buddha sculptured in a rock on the right side of G.T. road.

facts.text: Ghalegay was chosen as the first capital of Swat in 1849.
facts.quote: During the recent Pashtun era in 1849, when the first legal government was formed, Ghalegay was chosen as the first capital of Swat because of its suitable geographical location.

access: Roadside on the Mingora-Barikot road.

Italian excavation

facts.quote: is rectangular in plan, measuring 28m by 21m

facts.text: Considered the earliest mosque of northern Pakistan.
facts.quote: The mosque of Odigram date back to the period of Mahmud or his grandson Maudud (1041-50 A.D.) and is therefore to be considered to be the earliest of northern Pakistan.
